source.text: Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω, καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;

records.literal_gloss: Heard Jesus that they had thrown him out, and having found him he said, "You, do you believe in the Son of the man?"

en.L: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and having found him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
en.B: Jesus heard that they had thrown the man out, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
en.R: Jesus heard that the leaders had thrown the man out. So Jesus went and found him and asked, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"

es.L: Oyó Jesús que lo habían echado fuera, y hallándolo, le dijo: «¿Tú crees en el Hijo del Hombre?».
es.B: Jesús oyó que habían echado fuera al hombre, y cuando lo encontró, le dijo: «¿Crees tú en el Hijo del Hombre?».
es.R: Jesús oyó que los dirigentes habían echado fuera al hombre. Entonces fue a buscarlo y le preguntó: «¿Crees en el Hijo del Hombre?».

fr.L: Jésus entendit dire qu’ils l’avaient jeté dehors ; et, l’ayant trouvé, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Toi, crois-tu au Fils de l’homme ? »
fr.B: Jésus apprit qu’on avait jeté l’homme dehors, et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le trouva, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Et toi, crois-tu au Fils de l’homme ? »
fr.R: Jésus a appris que les chefs avaient jeté l’homme dehors. Alors Jésus est allé le trouver et lui a demandé : « Est-ce que tu crois au Fils de l’homme ? »

sw.L: Yesu alisikia kwamba wamemtupa nje, na alipomkuta, akasema, "Je, wewe unamwamini Mwana wa Adamu?"
sw.B: Yesu alisikia kwamba wamemtupa mtu yule nje, na alipomkuta, akamwambia, "Je, unamwamini Mwana wa Adamu?"
sw.R: Yesu alisikia kwamba viongozi walikuwa wamemfukuza mtu yule. Basi Yesu alikwenda akamtafuta, akamwuliza, "Je, unamwamini Mwana wa Adamu?"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nghe rằng họ đã đuổi anh ta ra ngoài, và khi gặp anh ta, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Anh có tin vào Con Người không?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nghe tin họ đã đuổi anh ta ra, nên khi gặp anh ta, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi: "Anh có tin vào Con Người không?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nghe tin các nhà lãnh đạo đã đuổi người ấy ra. Vậy Ngài đi tìm anh ta và hỏi: "Anh có tin vào Con Người không?"

ko.L: 예수께서 그들이 그를 밖으로 내쫓았다는 것을 들으시고, 그를 만나시자 말씀하셨다. "너는 인자를 믿느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서는 그들이 그 사람을 쫓아냈다는 말을 들으셨다. 그리고 그를 만나셨을 때 말씀하셨다. "너는 인자를 믿느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서는 지도자들이 그 사람을 쫓아냈다는 소식을 들으셨다. 그래서 그를 찾아가 만나서 물으셨다. "너는 인자, 곧 사람의 아들을 믿느냐?"

pt.L: Jesus ouviu que o tinham expulsado e, tendo-o encontrado, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Você crê no Filho do Homem?"
pt.B: Jesus soube que tinham expulsado o homem e, quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} o encontrou, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Você crê no Filho do Homem?"
pt.R: Jesus ouviu que os líderes tinham expulsado o homem. Então Jesus foi procurá-lo, encontrou-o e perguntou: "Você acredita no Filho do Homem?"

am.L: ኢየሱስ ወደ ውጭ እንዳባረሩት ሰማ፤ አግኝቶትም እንዲህ አለው፦ «አንተ በሰው ልጅ ታምናለህን?»
am.B: ኢየሱስ ሰውየውን እንዳባረሩት ሰማ፤ ባገኘውም ጊዜ እንዲህ አለው፦ «በሰው ልጅ ታምናለህ?»
am.R: ኢየሱስ መሪዎቹ ሰውየውን እንዳባረሩት ሰማ። ስለዚህ ኢየሱስ ሄዶ አገኘውና እንዲህ ብሎ ጠየቀው፦ «በሰው ልጅ ታምናለህ?»

hi.L: यीशु ने सुना कि उन्होंने उसे बाहर निकाल दिया है, और उसे पाकर उन्होंने कहा, "क्या तुम मनुष्य के पुत्र पर विश्वास करते हो?"
hi.B: यीशु ने सुना कि उन्होंने उस आदमी को बाहर निकाल दिया है, और जब वे उससे मिले, तो उन्होंने कहा, "क्या तुम मनुष्य के पुत्र पर विश्वास करते हो?"
hi.R: यीशु ने सुना कि अगुवों ने उस आदमी को बाहर निकाल दिया है। तब यीशु ने जाकर उसे ढूँढ़ा और पूछा, "क्या तुम मनुष्य के पुत्र पर विश्वास करते हो?"

ru.L: Услышал Иисус, что выгнали его вон, и, найдя его, сказал: «Ты веришь в Сына Человеческого?»
ru.B: Иисус услышал, что того человека выгнали, и, когда нашёл его, сказал: «Ты веришь в Сына Человеческого?»
ru.R: Иисус услышал, что вожди выгнали этого человека. Тогда Иисус пошёл, нашёл его и спросил: «Ты веришь в Сына Человеческого?»

uk.L: Ісус почув, що його вигнали геть, і, знайшовши його, сказав: «Ти віриш у Сина Людського?»
uk.B: Ісус почув, що того чоловіка вигнали, і, коли знайшов його, сказав: «Чи віриш ти в Сина Людського?»
uk.R: Ісус почув, що провідники вигнали чоловіка. Тож Ісус пішов, знайшов його і запитав: «Ти віриш у Сина Людського?»

ja.L: イエスは、彼らがその人を外に追い出したことを聞かれ、彼を見つけて言われた。「あなたは人の子を信じるか？」
ja.B: イエスは、彼らがその人を追い出したと聞かれ、彼を見つけて言われた。「あなたは人の子を信じるか？」
ja.R: イエスは、指導者たちがその人を追い出したことを聞かれました。そこでイエスはその人を捜して見つけ、尋ねられました。「あなたは人の子を信じるか？」

id.L: Yesus mendengar bahwa mereka telah mengusir dia, dan setelah menemukan dia, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata, "Engkau, percayakah engkau kepada Anak Manusia?"
id.B: Yesus mendengar bahwa mereka telah mengusir orang itu. Ketika {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} menemukan dia, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata, "Percayakah engkau kepada Anak Manusia?"
id.R: Yesus mendengar bahwa para pemimpin itu telah mengusir orang itu. Jadi Yesus pergi mencari dia, dan setelah menemukannya {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} bertanya, "Apakah kamu percaya kepada Anak Manusia?"

alternatives: the Son of God (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "the Son of God". The oldest witnesses, among them two early papyri, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "the Son of Man", the title Jesus uses of himself throughout John. A change from the unusual question about the Son of Man to the more familiar confession of the Son of God is easier to explain than the reverse. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they threw him out: the leaders drove him from their presence, and with it, in the light of 9:22, from the synagogue community
alternatives: they only sent him out of the room
a formal sentence of expulsion pronounced on the spot
decisions.reason: The words repeat the end of verse 34. They at least mean that the Pharisees put him out of their presence in contempt. John has already said that the authorities had agreed to put out of the synagogue anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ (9:22), so the reader is meant to see the man suffering what his parents feared. John does not describe any formal procedure.
As with the man healed at the pool (5:14), it is Jesus who finds the man after the healing. The one the authorities have thrown out is sought and received by Jesus (compare 6:37; 10:3-4).

decisions.choice: you, do you believe: the pronoun is emphatic
alternatives: a plain question with no stress on the person
decisions.reason: The Greek states "you" where the verb alone would do. It sets the man over against the Pharisees who have refused to believe: whatever they think, does he believe?

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's title for himself
alternatives: a general expression for a human being
decisions.reason: In John the Son of Man is the one who comes down from heaven and is lifted up (1:51; 3:13-14; 8:28), and the one to whom the Father has given authority to judge (5:27). That last point prepares for verse 39. The title draws on Daniel 7:13-14. The man does not yet know that Jesus is speaking of himself (verse 36).

Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including the pronouns for the Son of Man in verse 36, since the one asked about is Jesus (as with the coming Messiah at 4:25 and 7:27), and "you" when people speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: the leaders; So Jesus went and found him
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" were, the leaders who questioned the man in verses 13-34, and makes plain that Jesus went looking for him (meaning decision m3).
The emphatic "tú" (meaning decision m4) is the man and has no setting.
As in English: Readable names who "they" were and that Jesus sought the man out (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for this passage (9:35-41). The passé simple ("Jésus apprit", "il dit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus a appris"), the past tense young readers know. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("tu l’as vu", "je suis venu").

The pronoun "you" is written out in the Greek and sets the man against the Pharisees who refused to believe (meaning decision m4). French can stress it with a detached "toi" without strain, so Literal and Balanced show it; Readable keeps the plain question. "Croire au Fils" renders the Greek "believe into", as in 3:36.
An adult of unknown age; "anh" is the plain respectful form, as the neighbours and the leaders also use. "Con" would make Jesus his elder or teacher before the man has come to faith.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for Jesus in the narrative; plain "Ngài" at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: Only the capital letter changes with the setting.

alternatives: capitalised pronoun alternatives, as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and God is carried at every level by the subject honorific -si-, by "께서" and by "그분".

alternatives: "인자" alone, as at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: "인자" is the title at every level; Readable adds the plain-word gloss "사람의 아들" once in the passage, as the style guide allows, because the Sino-Korean title is opaque to new readers.

Jesus speaks to one person with "você" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); the written-out "você" carries the stress of the Greek pronoun (meaning decision m4). "Crer em" at Literal and Balanced, "acreditar em" at Readable, as the style guide's terms for "believe".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: "he" is in the verb ("አግኝቶት", "አለው")
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "በ... ማመን" (believe in) with the key term "ማመን" at every level
decisions.reason: "Believe" is a key term in John and stays the same verb at every level; Amharic marks "believe in" with the prefix "በ" ("በሰው ልጅ ታምናለህ").

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span; honorific "उन्होंने" for Jesus in the narrative
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is shown by the honorific third person at every level, as the style guide sets out. This holds for the whole passage.

Russian needs no subject pronoun with the verb here, so the English "he" with its setting has no counterpart. The pronouns for the Son of Man in 9:36-37 take the setting, since the one asked about is Jesus.
As the English Readable: Readable names who "they" were and shows that Jesus went looking for the man (m3).

records.literal_gloss: Answered that [one] and said, "And who is he, sir, that I may believe in him?"

en.L: That [man] answered and said, "And who is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, Sir, so that I may believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.B: The man answered, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, Sir? Tell me, so that I may believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: The man answered, "Sir, who is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}? I want to believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: Respondió aquel y dijo: «¿Y quién es, Señor, para que crea en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}?».
es.B: El hombre respondió: «¿Quién es, Señor? Dímelo, para que crea en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».
es.R: El hombre respondió: «Señor, ¿quién es? Quiero creer en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».

fr.L: Celui-là répondit et dit : « Et qui est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, Monsieur, pour que je croie en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ? »
fr.B: L’homme répondit : « Qui est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, Monsieur ? Dis-le-moi, pour que je croie en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »
fr.R: L’homme a répondu : « Monsieur, qui est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ? Je veux croire en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »

sw.L: Yule akajibu, akasema, "Naye ni nani, bwana, ili nipate kumwamini?"
sw.B: Mtu yule akajibu, "Ni nani huyo, bwana? Niambie, ili nipate kumwamini."
sw.R: Mtu yule akajibu, "Ni nani huyo, bwana? Nataka kumwamini."

vi.L: Người ấy đáp và nói: "Vậy Đấng ấy là ai, thưa ông, để tôi tin vào Đấng ấy?"
vi.B: Anh ta đáp: "Thưa ông, Đấng ấy là ai? Xin cho tôi biết để tôi tin vào Đấng ấy."
vi.R: Người ấy trả lời: "Thưa ông, Đấng ấy là ai? Tôi muốn tin vào Đấng ấy."

ko.L: 그 [사람]이 대답하여 말했다. "그러면 그분이 누구십니까, 선생님? 제가 그분을 믿을 수 있도록 말입니다."
ko.B: 그 사람이 대답했다. "선생님, 그분이 누구십니까? 말씀해 주십시오. 그러면 제가 그분을 믿겠습니다."
ko.R: 그 사람이 대답했다. "선생님, 그분이 누구십니까? 저는 그분을 믿고 싶습니다."

pt.L: Aquele [homem] respondeu e disse: "E quem é {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, senhor, para que eu creia {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}?"
pt.B: O homem respondeu: "Quem é {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, senhor? Quero saber, para crer {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}."
pt.R: O homem respondeu: "Senhor, quem é {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}? Eu quero acreditar {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}."

am.L: ያም [ሰው] መለሰ፤ እንዲህም አለ፦ «ጌታዬ፣ ታዲያ በእርሱ አምን ዘንድ እርሱ ማን ነው?»
am.B: ሰውየውም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «ጌታዬ፣ እርሱ ማን ነው? በእርሱ እንዳምን ንገረኝ።»
am.R: ሰውየውም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «ጌታዬ፣ እርሱ ማን ነው? በእርሱ ማመን እፈልጋለሁ።»

hi.L: उसने उत्तर दिया और कहा, "और वह कौन है, श्रीमान, कि मैं उस पर विश्वास करूँ?"
hi.B: उस आदमी ने उत्तर दिया, "महोदय, वह कौन है? मुझे बताइए, ताकि मैं उस पर विश्वास करूँ।"
hi.R: उस आदमी ने जवाब दिया, "साहब, वह कौन है? मैं उस पर विश्वास करना चाहता हूँ।"

ru.L: Ответил тот и сказал: «А кто {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}, господин, чтобы мне поверить в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}?»
ru.B: Человек ответил: «Кто {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}, господин? Скажи мне, чтобы я мог поверить в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}.»
ru.R: Человек ответил: «Господин, кто {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}? Я хочу поверить в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}.»

uk.L: Той відповів і сказав: «А хто {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}}, пане, щоб я повірив у {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}?»
uk.B: Чоловік відповів: «Хто {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}}, пане? Скажи мені, щоб я міг повірити в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}.»
uk.R: Чоловік відповів: «Пане, а хто {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}}? Я хочу повірити в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}.»

ja.L: その人は答えて言った。「主よ、その方はどなたですか？わたしがその方を信じることができるように。」
ja.B: その人は答えた。「先生、その方はどなたですか？教えてください。その方を信じたいのです。」
ja.R: その人は答えました。「先生、その方はどなたですか？わたしはその方を信じたいのです。」

id.L: Orang itu menjawab dan berkata, "Siapakah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, Tuan, supaya saya percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}?"
id.B: Orang itu menjawab, "Siapakah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, Tuan? Katakanlah, supaya saya percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}."
id.R: Orang itu menjawab, "Tuan, siapakah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}? Saya mau percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}."

alternatives: Lord, a confession of who Jesus is
decisions.reason: The word is the polite form used to anyone of standing, as the Samaritan woman uses it (4:11, 15, 19). The man already holds Jesus to be a prophet (9:17) and sent from God (9:33), but he does not yet know who the Son of Man is, or that he is speaking to him. In verse 38, once he believes, the same word carries the full sense of "Lord". A footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: and who is he, so that I may believe: an eager question; he is ready to believe once he knows
decisions.reason: The opening "and" gives the question urgency, and the clause of purpose shows why he asks: he wants to know whom to believe in. He does not refuse the question; he asks to be shown.

decisions.choice: he and him: the Son of Man, who is Jesus himself
decisions.reason: The man asks about a third person, but the reader knows the answer, and verse 37 gives it: the one he is speaking to.
Shows the polite address (meaning decision m1), so that the change to "Lord" in verse 38 can be seen.
Balanced breaks the question in two and supplies "Tell me", which the clause of purpose implies (meaning decision m2).

Here "señor" is the polite address (meaning decision m1); in 9:38 the same word becomes "Lord" as the man believes. English shows the change with "Sir" and "Lord"; Spanish keeps one word, as the Greek does, and the footnote points it out.
As in English: supplies what the clause of purpose implies (meaning decision m2).

The same Greek word is a polite "Sir" before the man believes and "Lord" once he does (meaning decision m1 here, m2 at 9:38). French follows the book's choice: "Monsieur" for someone who does not yet know who Jesus is, "Seigneur" for one who believes, so the change the English shows is visible in French too. The man says "tu" to Jesus, as everyone does.

decisions.choice: you have seen him: the man who was blind has now seen the Son of Man

decisions.choice: the one speaking with you is he: Jesus reveals himself as he did to the Samaritan woman
decisions.reason: The words echo 4:26, where Jesus tells the woman that the Messiah she expects is the one speaking with her. In both places Jesus makes himself known to someone who has asked.

decisions.choice: both ... and: two ways of meeting him, seeing and hearing
alternatives: the first "and" as a mere connective
decisions.reason: The paired "and ... and" joins the two clauses: he has seen him, and he is hearing him now. The emphatic "that one" points from the Son of Man asked about to the speaker.
Literal keeps the Greek pointing word "that one" at the end; Balanced turns it round to the natural order.

decisions.choice: the words are part of the text (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the words "He said, 'I believe, Lord,' and he worshiped him. And Jesus said" (verses 38 and the start of 39) are missing
decisions.reason: A few early witnesses, among them an early papyrus (P75), the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex W, lack this verse and the opening words of verse 39, so that Jesus's words in verse 39 follow straight on from verse 37. Almost all other manuscripts have them, and the SBLGNT prints them. A footnote notes the omission. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord: now an address of faith
alternatives: Sir, a polite address as in verse 36
decisions.reason: It is the same word the man used in verse 36, but he now says it as he confesses his faith in the Son of Man. Those who have come to believe call Jesus "Lord" (6:68; 11:27; 20:28). The word is the same; what has changed is the man who says it.

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down before him in worship
alternatives: knelt before him in respect, as before an honored human
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down before someone, and it can be used of homage to a human superior (Matthew 18:26). In John, though, it is used only of worshiping God (4:20-24; 12:20), and here it follows a confession of faith in the Son of Man. A footnote gives "knelt before him".

decisions.choice: I believe: the end of the man's journey from blindness to faith
decisions.reason: Step by step the man has spoken of "the man called Jesus" (9:11), "a prophet" (9:17) and one "from God" (9:33); now he believes and worships. The Pharisees have moved the other way, from questions to rejection, as verses 39-41 bring out.
The address changes from "Sir" (verse 36) to "Lord" because the man now believes (meaning decision m2).
Readable shows the bodily act the verb describes as well as its sense (meaning decision m3).

uk.R: Ісус сказав: «Я прийшов у цей світ, щоб звершити суд. Я прийшов, щоб сліпі бачили, а ті, хто думає, що бачить, стали сліпими.»

ja.L: そしてイエスは言われた。「裁きのために、わたしはこの世に来た。見ない者たちが見るようになり、見る者たちが目の見えない者となるためである。」
ja.B: イエスは言われた。「わたしがこの世に来たのは、裁きをもたらすためである。見えない者は見えるようになり、見える者は見えなくなる。」
ja.R: イエスは言われました。「わたしは裁きをもたらすために、この世に来た。目の見えない人が見えるようになり、見えると思っている人が見えなくなるためだ。」

id.L: Lalu Yesus berkata, "Untuk penghakiman {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} datang ke dalam dunia ini, supaya mereka yang tidak melihat dapat melihat, dan mereka yang melihat menjadi buta."
id.B: Yesus berkata, "Aku datang ke dunia ini untuk menghakimi, supaya mereka yang tidak dapat melihat menjadi dapat melihat, dan mereka yang dapat melihat menjadi buta."
id.R: Yesus berkata, "Aku datang ke dunia ini untuk menghakimi. Aku datang supaya orang-orang yang buta dapat melihat, dan orang-orang yang merasa dapat melihat menjadi buta."

decisions.choice: judgment: a verdict that separates people, brought about by his coming
alternatives: condemnation as the aim of his coming
the act of judging in a court
decisions.reason: The word is the result of judging, a verdict. Here it is the division that Jesus's coming brings about between those who come to see and those who refuse to.

decisions.choice: his coming brings judgment, though he did not come to condemn
decisions.reason: In 3:17 God did not send the Son to judge the world but to save it, and in 12:47 Jesus says the same. Yet the Father has given all judgment to the Son (5:22, 27), and 3:19 explains how both are true: the light has come, and people's response to it is itself the judgment. Here the man who was blind has come to the light, and the Pharisees have turned from it.

decisions.choice: so that: the purpose of his coming, which is also its outcome
decisions.reason: The conjunction normally states a purpose. Jesus came to give sight; that those who claim to see become blind is the other side of the same coming, as light that shows the way also exposes those who turn away from it (3:19-21).

decisions.choice: giving sight to the blind and blinding those who see: echoes of Isaiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah promises that the eyes of the blind will be opened (Isaiah 29:18; 35:5; 42:7), and speaks of a people who see but do not perceive, whose eyes are shut (Isaiah 6:9-10, quoted in John 12:40; compare 42:18-19).

decisions.choice: seeing and blindness in two senses: the body's eyes and understanding of God
decisions.reason: The whole chapter turns on this. The man born blind receives his sight and comes to see who Jesus is; the Pharisees, who can see and claim to know (9:24, 29), become blind to him. Those who "see" are those who think they see (verse 41).
Balanced and Readable say plainly what "for judgment" means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: people who think they can see
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit that the seeing is claimed, as Jesus says in verse 41 (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: para hacer juicio (B); para traer juicio (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: says what "for judgment" means (meaning decision m1).
As in English: the seeing is claimed (meaning decision m5).
As the English Readable, Readable makes plain that the seeing is claimed (meaning decision m5; verse 41). French "croire voir" says "think they see" in two words.

decisions.choice: the purpose clause after the main verb ("... መጣሁ፤ የማያዩ እንዲያዩ ...")
alternatives: the purpose clause first, as at Balanced
decisions.reason: Amharic usually puts a purpose clause before its verb; Literal keeps the Greek order of the clauses, which Amharic allows as an added explanation, and Balanced uses the usual order.
"裁くために" would say that he came to condemn, against 3:17. The judgment is the verdict his coming brings about (m1, m2), so Balanced and Readable say he came to bring it.

fr.B: Quelques Pharisiens qui étaient avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} entendirent cela et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Tu ne veux pas dire que nous aussi, nous sommes aveugles ? »
fr.R: Quelques Pharisiens qui étaient là avec Jésus ont entendu cela. Ils ont dit à Jésus : « Tu ne dis quand même pas que nous sommes aveugles, nous aussi ? »

ru.B: Некоторые из фарисеев, которые были с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, услышали это и сказали {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}: «Ты ведь не хочешь сказать, что и мы слепые?»
ru.R: Некоторые фарисеи, которые были там с Иисусом, услышали это. Они сказали Иисусу: «Ты ведь не говоришь, что мы тоже слепые?»

uk.B: Деякі з фарисеїв, що були з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, почули це й сказали {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}}: «Ти ж не хочеш сказати, що й ми сліпі?»
uk.R: Деякі фарисеї, які були там з Ісусом, почули це. Вони сказали Ісусові: «Ти ж не кажеш, що й ми сліпі?»

ja.L: イエスと共にいたファリサイ派の人々のうち[何人か]が、これらのことを聞いて、イエスに言った。「まさか、我々も目が見えない[と言う]のではないだろう？」

ja.R: そこにイエスと一緒にいたファリサイ派の人々の何人かが、これを聞きました。彼らはイエスに言いました。「まさか、我々まで目が見えないと言うつもりではないだろうな？」

id.L: [Beberapa] dari orang-orang Farisi yang berada bersama-sama dengan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} mendengar hal itu dan berkata kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, "Apakah kami juga buta?"
id.B: Beberapa orang Farisi yang ada bersama {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} mendengar hal itu dan berkata kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, "Engkau tidak bermaksud bahwa kami juga buta, bukan?"
id.R: Beberapa orang Farisi yang ada di situ bersama Yesus mendengar hal itu. Mereka berkata kepada Yesus, "Engkau tidak bermaksud mengatakan bahwa kami juga buta, kan?"

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question begins with a particle that looks for a denial. The Pharisees do not ask whether they are blind; they object that Jesus cannot be saying so.

decisions.choice: we too: we as well as others he calls blind
decisions.reason: The stress falls on "we": they assume that blindness belongs to people like the man they have just called a sinner (9:34), not to teachers of the Law.

decisions.choice: who were with him: who were present with Jesus at the time
decisions.reason: The phrase means only that they were there. These Pharisees were not his disciples (9:28); they heard what he said to the man.

decisions.choice: You do not mean that ... do you? (B); You are not saying that ... are you? (R)
decisions.reason: The English puts the expected "no" into the question (meaning decision m1).
The Greek says "of the Pharisees", meaning some of them; Literal brackets the supplied word.
Puts the expected "no" into the question (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Est-ce que nous aussi, nous serions aveugles ?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no (meaning decision m1). The French conditional of indignation ("nous serions aveugles ?") gives that in Literal without adding words; Balanced and Readable put the expected "no" into the question, as the English does.

decisions.choice: The Pharisees speak to Jesus in the plain style without honorifics (-느냐)
decisions.reason: The style guide allows open opponents to address Jesus without honorifics where the scene is hostile; these are the men who have just thrown out the man Jesus healed. The narrator keeps the honorific (그분께).
As in 9:13-34: "ዕውር" is the plain written word, and Readable uses the gentler everyday "ዓይነ ስውር" for both the physical and the figurative blindness, so that the play on the two stays visible.

alternatives: a plain question "我々も目が見えないのか"
decisions.reason: The question looks for a denial (m1); "まさか" with "ではないだろう" gives that, in the plain speech the Pharisees use to Jesus.

source.text: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ τυφλοὶ ἦτε, οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν· νῦν δὲ λέγετε ὅτι Βλέπομεν· ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑμῶν μένει.

records.literal_gloss: Said to them the Jesus, "If blind you were, not would you have sin; now but you say that, 'We see'; the sin of you remains."

en.L: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would not have sin; but now you say, 'We see'; your sin remains."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But you say, 'We can see,' so your sin remains."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would not be guilty of sin. But you say, 'We can see.' So your sin remains."

es.L: Jesús les dijo: «Si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} ciegos, no {{plural_you:tendrían|tendríais}} pecado; pero ahora {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “Vemos”; {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} pecado permanece».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «Si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} ciegos, no {{plural_you:tendrían|tendríais}} pecado. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: “Vemos”, así que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} pecado permanece».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} ciegos, no {{plural_you:serían culpables|seríais culpables}} de pecado. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: “Podemos ver”. Así que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} pecado permanece».

fr.L: Jésus leur dit : « Si vous étiez aveugles, vous n’auriez pas de péché ; mais maintenant vous dites : “Nous voyons” ; votre péché demeure. »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Si vous étiez aveugles, vous seriez sans péché. Mais vous dites : “Nous voyons”, alors votre péché demeure. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Si vous étiez aveugles, vous ne seriez pas coupables de péché. Mais vous dites : “Nous voyons bien.” Alors votre péché reste sur vous. »

ru.L: Сказал им Иисус: «Если бы вы были слепы, не имели бы греха; теперь же говорите: “Видим”; грех ваш остаётся.»
ru.B: Иисус сказал им: «Если бы вы были слепыми, на вас не было бы греха. Но вы говорите: “Мы видим”, — поэтому ваш грех остаётся.»

ja.L: イエスは彼らに言われた。「もしあなたがたが目の見えない者であったなら、罪はなかったであろう。しかし今、あなたがたは『我々は見える』と言っている。あなたがたの罪はとどまる。」
ja.B: イエスは彼らに言われた。「目が見えなかったのであれば、あなたがたに罪はなかったであろう。しかしあなたがたは今、『見える』と言っている。だから、あなたがたの罪はとどまっている。」
ja.R: イエスは彼らに言われました。「もしあなたたちが目の見えない者だったなら、罪を問われることはなかった。しかし、あなたたちは『見える』と言っている。だから、あなたたちの罪はとどまっている。」

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: they are not blind in the way that would excuse them
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes that the condition is not true. They are not people who cannot see; they claim to see.

decisions.choice: to have sin: to be guilty of sin
decisions.reason: John uses the phrase for guilt that a person must answer for (15:22, 24; 19:11). Those who truly could not see would not be held guilty for failing to see.

decisions.choice: their sin is claiming sight while refusing it
alternatives: they are guilty because of what they know
decisions.reason: The Pharisees claim to know (9:24, 29) and yet refuse the light that has come (3:19-20). Their claim to see leaves them no excuse; in the same way Jesus says that those who do not believe will die in their sins (8:24).

decisions.choice: remains: stays on them and is not taken away
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John uses for what lasts. As God's wrath remains on whoever refuses to obey the Son (3:36), so their sin remains, because they turn from the one who takes away the sin of the world (1:29).
